### Shot-by-Shot (Tickets Delivered: 4)

| Ticket | Club | Result | Hazards | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| S260-1 | Long Iron | Green | -- | New src/cli/guards/command-parse.ts segments a Bash invocation into commands and argv tokens, tracking each token's byte span. commandMatches() requires the program and subcommand words to be unquoted, so `echo "gh pr merge"` never matches. Leading env assignments are skipped so `GH_TOKEN=x gh pr merge` still resolves. |
| S260-2 | Long Iron | Green | Rough: First cut mis-parsed the `<<<` herestring: the leading `<` fell through to a token, then the second and third `<` matched the two-character heredoc test, so the herestring's argument was consumed as a heredoc delimiter and the rest of the command vanished. Fixed by counting the full `<` run before deciding. Caught by a test written for the case, not by review. | The scanner honours single quotes, double quotes with backslash escapes, line continuations, and heredoc bodies (quoted, unquoted and `<<-` tab-stripped delimiters). A heredoc body is skipped entirely rather than tokenized, so documentation *about* a flag can never read as passing it. An unterminated heredoc swallows the remainder, matching the shell. |
| S260-3 | Short Iron | Green | Rough: The `--flag=value` head split has to be restricted to long flags. Applying it to short flags re-created the original bug from the other direction: `cut -d=` splits to `-d` and matches. Short flags take their value adjacently, long flags take it after `=`. | findFlagToken matches whole tokens (or a `--flag=value` head), skips quoted tokens, and stops at a bare `--`. removeToken splices the token plus its preceding whitespace out of the ORIGINAL string, so the suggestion differs from what the operator typed only by the flag — the previous non-global regex replace rewrote the first match anywhere, including inside prose being written to a file. |
| S260-4 | Short Iron | Green | Bunker: version-check was the worst of the remaining set and was not in the issue: `command.includes('git push')` AND `/(main|master)/` over the raw text, gating a deny. Any command mentioning both strings — a release note, an issue body, a heredoc — was blocked from running. It also fired on a branch merely containing 'main', e.g. feat/maintenance. | Ten guards read tool_input.command; three deny on a raw-text match and were converted: version-check, worktree-self-remove and worktree-merge, plus branch-before-commit. pr-review, post-push and push-nudge are advisory (no deny) and push-nudge already anchors to command position; phase-boundary already tokenizes with its own splitter; shell-write matches raw text by design, since detecting heredocs and inline interpreters is its whole purpose. |

### Hazards Discovered

| Type | Ticket | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Rough | S260-2 | First cut mis-parsed the `<<<` herestring: the leading `<` fell through to a token, then the second and third `<` matched the two-character heredoc test, so the herestring's argument was consumed as a heredoc delimiter and the rest of the command vanished. Fixed by counting the full `<` run before deciding. Caught by a test written for the case, not by review. |
| Rough | S260-3 | The `--flag=value` head split has to be restricted to long flags. Applying it to short flags re-created the original bug from the other direction: `cut -d=` splits to `-d` and matches. Short flags take their value adjacently, long flags take it after `=`. |
| Bunker | S260-4 | version-check was the worst of the remaining set and was not in the issue: `command.includes('git push')` AND `/(main|master)/` over the raw text, gating a deny. Any command mentioning both strings — a release note, an issue body, a heredoc — was blocked from running. It also fired on a branch merely containing 'main', e.g. feat/maintenance. |

**Known hazards for future sprints:**
- Any guard matching a flag or phrase against the raw Bash invocation will fire on commands that merely carry the text as data — issue bodies, commit messages, heredocs writing documentation. Parse to argv tokens instead; src/cli/guards/command-parse.ts exists for this.
- A guard that rewrites the command it blocks must splice the original string by byte span. A regex replace over raw text edits the first match anywhere, so following the guard's own advice can silently corrupt file content.
